sources.title: Mary Kom (Q328951) -- verified live via the Wikidata API (2026-10-26): English label 'Mary Kom', description 'Indian amateur boxer', citizenship India, listed birth date 1982-03-01 (Olympedia and press ages give 1 March 1983; the candidate uses 1983), P18 image 'Mary Kom - British High Commission, Delhi, 27 July 2011.jpg', no Korean label. Orientation only; not used as support for any row.

Olympedia, 'Mary Kom' athlete record (olympedia.org), read in full: full name Mangte Chungneijang 'Mary' Kom, nickname 'Magnificent Mary', born 1 March 1983 in Kangathei, Churachanpur, Manipur; flyweight bronze at the 2012 London Olympics, ninth in 2020 (held 2021); closing-ceremony flagbearer 2012 and opening-ceremony flagbearer 2020; Asian Games bronze 2010 and gold 2014, Commonwealth Games gold 2018 (48 kg). CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE. Database record, factual, no behavioural detail.

Rajashree Rath, 'Mary Kom: Punching above her weight' (Al Jazeera English, 21 October 2013; web.archive.org copy), read in full: feature from her boxing academy in Imphal; five-time world champion and Olympic medallist; her start at a Sports Authority of India centre after seeing a state boxer win Asian Games gold in 1998, the coach Ibomcha Singh's first refusal and her persistence at the gate; her academy run since 2006 with free lodging and training for promising poor trainees (62 trainees, more than half girls); one of the inspirations for women's boxing at London 2012; her stated 2016 target. Family, marriage, bereavement and income passages deliberately not used. Journalistic feature with named trainees; admiring.

Abhijeet Kulkarni, 'For Mary Kom, life comes second to Olympic dream' (Firstpost, 23 May 2012; web.archive.org copy), read in full: sports-journalist profile after her Olympic qualification; she became the first Indian woman to qualify for Olympic boxing, relying on a favourable semifinal result after losing to Nicola Adams; her return in 2008 to win a fourth successive world title despite talk of decline, her 2009 national-championship loss to a 19-year-old and public complaint against officials, her move up from 48 kg to 51 kg for the Olympics, and about 300 days a year in national camps. Family and health passages deliberately not used. Journalistic, mixed (admiring with a note of her outburst).

Gregg Bakowski, 'Nicola Adams beats Mary Kom to reach 51kg Olympic final' (The Guardian live blog, 8 August 2012; web.archive.org copy), read in full on Kom: round-by-round account of the London 2012 flyweight semifinal she lost 11-6 to Great Britain's Nicola Adams, which gave her the bronze; says Adams looked too big and physical for her and that Kom looked clumsy overextending to reach Adams; Kom raised her work rate in the last round to close the gap. Independent British live commentary; critical of her performance on the day; Adams' family remarks not used.

HT Correspondent, 'MC Mary Kom gets AIBA's Legends Award, Vikas Krishnan wins Best Boxer trophy' (Hindustan Times, 21 December 2016; web.archive.org copy), read in full: first AIBA Legends Award at the federation's 70th anniversary in Montreux; her return to the 48 kg division amid speculation it would join the 2020 Olympic programme, her stated intention to keep competing for three or four years and to aim for the 2018 Asian and Commonwealth Games and, if 48 kg was included, a 2020 Olympic gold; that Parliament sessions had kept her out of the Nationals (political duty not scored). Indian national daily; largely admiring.

B Shrikant, 'Mary Kom, Gaurav Solanki lead India's medal rush' (Hindustan Times, 14 April 2018; web.archive.org copy), read in full: her 5-0 win over Northern Ireland's Kristina O'Hara in the 2018 Commonwealth Games 48 kg final at age 35, in a field of eight, as the favourite with superior technique and experience; the writer's note that people had asked whether she still had the hunger against rivals nearly a decade younger; her thanks to coaches. Journalistic match report; admiring, with a caveat about the weak field.

Gaurav Bhatt, 'Mary Kom wins record sixth World Championships gold' (The Indian Express, 25 November 2018; web.archive.org copy), read in full: at 35 she became the first woman boxer to win six World Championship golds, a 5-0 win at 48 kg over Ukraine's Hanna Okhota in Delhi, equalling the Cuban Felix Savon's total of six; coach Chhote Lal Yadav on her tears afterward and her words that it was all for India; that her previous world medal had been in 2010. Journalistic report with a named coach; admiring.

Jonathan Selvaraj, 'Nikhat Zareen demands selection trial against Mary Kom amid unclear BFI rules' (ESPN, 17 October 2019), read in full on the selection dispute: after Kom's 2019 world bronze, the Boxing Federation of India hinted she might skip trials for the Olympic qualifiers; Nikhat Zareen wrote to the sports minister asking for a trial; the report finds the federation's own criteria unclear, and carries Kom's stated position that she sought an exemption but did not strong-arm the federation. Used only for the public selection-process dispute; the federation's rules, not Kom's character, are the story. Independent sports journalism; both sides quoted.

Press Information Bureau (Government of India), Copyright Policy page (pib.gov.in/content/137_2_CopyrightPolicy.aspx, Hindi page), and the Commons file page for 'Padma Vibhushan Mary Kom.jpg' (source: PIB photo gallery, President's Secretariat, 8 November 2021), checked for the portrait lead: the PIB policy says material may be reproduced free without prior permission but that authority should be obtained from the concerned department or copyright holder, reproduced accurately and with the source acknowledged. Not used for any scoring.

persistence.rationale: [src_komm_firstpost, src_komm_indianexpress, src_komm_hindustan2018, src_komm_aljazeera | 1998-2018 | journalism x4] Al Jazeera reports she returned to a coach's gate after being turned away, Firstpost that she came back in 2008 to win a fourth world title after talk she was finished and kept pushing for the Olympics through a 2009 setback, and the Indian Express and HT report a sixth world gold and a Commonwealth gold at age 35 against younger rivals. Sources are independent outlets and largely admiring, but the pattern of repeated comebacks is consistent across a decade; coach and quotations are Kom's own in places.

adaptability.rationale: [src_komm_firstpost, src_komm_hindustan2016, src_komm_olympedia | 2010-2018 | journalism x2 + database] Firstpost says she moved from 48 kg to 51 kg for the Olympics, and HT says she went back to 48 kg amid speculation about the 2020 programme; Olympedia lists medals in both divisions (Asian Games 51 kg gold 2014, Commonwealth 48 kg gold 2018). The weight-class changes are factual and corroborated; how she managed each change is described only briefly.

achievement_drive.rationale: [src_komm_hindustan2016, src_komm_aljazeera, src_komm_firstpost | 2012-2016 | journalism x3] She stated targets repeatedly: gold at Rio 2016 (Al Jazeera), more years of competing and a 2020 Olympic gold if 48 kg was included (HT), and Firstpost says she gave up much in pursuit of the Olympic dream. Targets are her own statements to reporters; results show she also followed through to a world and Commonwealth gold.

discipline.rationale: [src_komm_firstpost, src_komm_aljazeera | 2012-2013 | journalism x2] Firstpost reports she spent around 300 days a year in national camps; Al Jazeera shows her running a regular morning training session. The training load is from one outlet and the day-to-day routine is not described, hence an inference.

competitiveness.rationale: [src_komm_olympedia, src_komm_indianexpress, src_komm_guardian | 2012-2018 | database + journalism x2] The record (six world golds, Asian Games and Commonwealth golds, Olympic bronze) shows sustained success, and the Guardian shows her pushing her work rate in a losing semifinal; but results are an outcome, not a direct description of competitive drive, so this stays a strong inference.

impact_motivation.rationale: [src_komm_aljazeera | 2006-2013 | journalism] Al Jazeera reports that she and her husband ran a boxing academy in Imphal since 2006 offering free lodging and training to promising poor trainees, with 62 trainees. One outlet, without independent description of the academy, so confidence is low.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: [src_komm_firstpost, src_komm_espn | 2009-2019 | journalism x2] Firstpost records a public complaint in 2009 that officials were trying to end her career, and ESPN reports a 2019 selection row in which she sought exemption from trials and said she did not strong-arm the federation. Both are public sports-administration disputes with the other side's account partly absent; the score reflects willingness to dispute officials, not a judgement of who was right.

portrait.reason: No rights-clear portrait could be confirmed after one bounded retry. (1) The Wikidata P18 file 'Mary Kom - British High Commission, Delhi, 27 July 2011.jpg' (1307 x 1813, tagged OGL v1.0) rests only on an emailed permission ticket from the British High Commission with no Flickr or photo-level page found, and the event date is reported as 28 July by a news agency; rejected. (2) Government of India press photos on Commons (GODL-India), e.g. 'Padma Vibhushan Mary Kom.jpg' (8 November 2021, President's Secretariat, 1737 x 1591, no licence review), come from the PIB gallery whose policy allows free reproduction but says authority should be obtained from the concerned department; this is not a clear stated licence for the photo. A tight crop of her was saved at public/portraits/mary-kom-pib-2021.jpg (800 x 1261, native pixels, not used). (3) A CC0 selfie-style file by an uploader is identified only by its title. Next step: the lead may accept the PIB government-work basis for the saved crop, or obtain a photo with an explicit licence (for example a Flickr or Olympics media image with stated terms).

provenance.notes: PREFLIGHT: QID verified live (Wikidata wbgetentities 2026-10-26): Q328951, label 'Mary Kom', description 'Indian amateur boxer', no ko label; lead's hint confirmed. Birth: Wikidata 1982-03-01 but Olympedia gives 1 March 1983 and press ages (33 in Dec 2016, 35 in Nov 2018) agree with 1983; birthYear set to 1983. No existing candidate or src reference for slug mary-kom or QID Q328951 (searched data-pipeline, src, docs). Region south_asia (India). ZERO POLITICS: her 2016 Rajya Sabha nomination and any parliamentary or ministry roles are not scored; HT's remark that Parliament sessions kept her from the Nationals and Al Jazeera's health-ministry anti-drug campaign are not used. LIVING: public documented professional behaviour only; marriage, children, family, bereavement, religion, income and the 2025 separation coverage deliberately excluded. Vocabulary reused from existing athlete candidates: athlete, sport, athletic, cultural, competitor, sustained_excellence, competitive_performer (labels exist). CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: Olympedia athlete record (https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/122492), cross-checked against the Indian Express six-title report and HT 2018. portrait_preflight: plausible (lead) / not confirmed: the OGL file rests on emailed permission only and the PIB government photos carry a conditional notice, so the portrait is HELD (see portrait.reason). READ (9 cited non-Wikidata sources plus the PIB policy page): Olympedia, Al Jazeera 2013, Firstpost 2012, Guardian live blog 2012, HT 2016, HT 2018, Indian Express 2018, ESPN 2019, PIB policy. NOT OPENED: Olympics.com athlete page (connection refused), IBA/AIBA site, BBC and Guardian long profiles (guessed URLs 404), NDTV 2012 (error page), her autobiography and film (self/dramatised), Wikipedia. PERSPECTIVES: reference database (Olympedia), Indian national press (HT, Indian Express, Firstpost), international press (Al Jazeera, Guardian), investigative-style sports journalism with both sides (ESPN). COUNTER-VOICES: Guardian's critical description of her semifinal performance; Firstpost's note of her public outburst against officials; ESPN's account of Zareen's challenge and the unclear federation rules; HT's caveat that the Commonwealth field was small. LIMITS: most behavioural material is admiring Indian press; coach and trainee voices are quoted second-hand; no insider or adversarial biography was available, so no score exceeds 76 and no confidence exceeds 0.62. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): rows reviewed: persistence, adaptability, conflict_tolerance. No row lowered: persistence and adaptability are corroborated by independent outlets and the factual record, and conflict_tolerance was already scored low with explicit caveats. No broad profile problem to flag, but the profile is sparse (7 rows) by design.
